marks.gloss_en: וכדרבי שמעון בן לקיש: אל תקרי שברת אלא שרבבת -- the teeth of the wicked were lengthened, as Og's were
he wanted to pull it off; his teeth were drawn out to this side and that, and he could not pull it off
בשלמא כולהו ניסא, אלא אשתו של לוט פורענותא הוא! -- all the other items are miracles, but Lot's wife is a punishment: why give thanks over her?
דאמר ברוך דיין האמת -- over her he says 'the true Judge' (= p_ishto_dayan_haemet)
[over Lot's wife] he says 'Blessed... the true Judge'
והא הודאה ושבח קתני! -- the baraita says that over all of them one gives thanks and praise, and 'the true Judge' is neither

תני: על לוט ועל אשתו מברכים שתים -- על אשתו אומר ברוך דיין האמת, ועל לוט אומר ברוך זוכר את הצדיקים: emend the baraita; the thanks-and-praise is over Lot (= p_tni_lot_veishto_shtayim, p_tni_al_lot_zocher)
(emend the baraita to) teach: over Lot and his wife one recites two blessings

the Emorites hid in caves in the mountains to kill Israel; when the ark came the mountains closed on one another and killed them, and their blood ran down into the streams of Arnon; Et and Hev saw the blood and told Israel, who sang
the tanna: [Elgavish = al gav ish] stones that stood [suspended] on account of a man and came down on account of a man
the stone Og king of Bashan sought to throw on Israel -- it is known by received tradition [not from a verse]
Moses was ten cubits tall; he took a ten-cubit axe, leapt ten cubits, struck Og on the ankle and killed him
the stone Moses sat on: as it is written, 'Moses' hands were heavy, and they took a stone and put it under him and he sat on it' (Ex 17:12)
Lot's wife: as it says, 'his wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt' (Gen 19:26)
יורדי הים מנלן? דכתיב... ואומר... יודו לה' חסדו

whence seafarers? 'they who go down to the sea in ships... they saw the works of the Lord' (Ps 107:23-24), and the storm, their reeling, their crying to the Lord, the calm, their gladness, and 'let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (107:25-31)
הולכי מדברות מנלן? דכתיב: תעו במדבר... יודו לה' חסדו

whence desert travellers? 'they wandered in the wilderness, in a desolate way, they found no inhabited city... they cried to the Lord... He led them on a straight way... let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (Ps 107:4-8)
מי שחלה ונתרפא, דכתיב: אוילים מדרך פשעם... יודו לה' חסדו

one who was ill and recovered: 'fools, because of their transgression... their soul abhorred all food... they cried to the Lord... He sent His word and healed them... let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (Ps 107:17-21)
מי שהיה חבוש בבית האסורין מנלן? דכתיב: ישבי חשך וצלמות... יודו לה' חסדו

whence one imprisoned? 'those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death... because they rebelled against the words of God', and 'He humbled their heart with toil', 'they cried to the Lord', 'He brought them out of darkness', 'let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (Ps 107:10-15)
Abaye's own verse: דכתיב וירוממוהו בקהל עם
Mar Zutra's own verse: שנאמר ובמושב זקנים יהללוהו
what does he bless? Rav Yehuda: 'Blessed ... who bestows good kindnesses'
מתקיף לה רב אשי: ואימא כולהו רבנן! -- say that all ten must be Sages
מי כתיב בקהל זקנים? בקהל עם כתיב -- the verse says 'the congregation of the PEOPLE', not 'of elders'
והא אמר אביי בעי אודויי באפי עשרה! -- Abaye said thanks must be given before ten (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)
דהוו בי עשרה -- there were ten there
והא איהו לא קא מודה! -- but he himself did not give thanks
לא צריך, דעני בתרייהו אמן -- he need not, for he answered amen after them
four must give thanks: seafarers
the visitors to Rav Yehuda: 'Blessed is the Merciful One who gave you to us and did not give you to the dust'
וחומת יריחו נבלעה? והא נפלה! -- was the wall swallowed? the verse says it fell
כיון דפותיה ורומה כי הדדי נינהו, משום הכי אבלעה בלועי -- since its width and its height were equal, therefore it was swallowed
it fell, as it says: 'when the people heard the sound of the shofar and shouted a great shout, the wall fell down in its place' (Josh 6:20)

והמאריך בתפלתו מעליותא היא? והאמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: כל המאריך בתפלתו ומעיין בה סוף בא לידי כאב לב; ואמר רבי יצחק: ...ועיון תפלה [recalls sins] -- is prolonging prayer a virtue? (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest; R' Yitzchak's dictum, p_iyun_tefilla_mazkir_avonot, is a second source the format cannot attach)
Rav Yehuda: three things, whoever prolongs them has his days and years prolonged -- one who prolongs his prayer
a sick person requires guarding
